Seminar Title:

Active Polymer Model to Understand 3D Chromosome Organization and Dynamics

Seminar Type:

Soudamini Sahoo

Abstract:

Chromatin organization inside the cell nucleus plays a crucial role in regulating gene expression and genome function. In this work, we model chromatin as an active polymer immersed in an
explicit solvent to study its structural and dynamical properties and to understand how active forces and hydrodynamic interactions (HI) regulate chromosome organization and dynamics.
The polymer consists of interacting monomers represented as transcriptionally active (TA) and transcriptionally inactive (TI) beads, connected by harmonic springs and subject to Lennard-
Jones interactions. Active forces are represented as non-equilibrium forces acting along the DNA backbone, mimicking the action of ATP-consuming molecular motors. Activity inspired
from ATP-driven activities is implemented as active forces only acting on TA beads, while hydrodynamic interactions are incorporated using Multi-particle collision dynamics (MPCD)
method. We investigate how varying activity strengths influence polymer conformation and dynamics. Our preliminary results show an interesting non-monotonic effect of activity on
polymer conformation. Hydrodynamic interactions are highlighted in the presence of activity. We are studying the combined effect of activity on the non-equilibrium 3D chromatin
organization and dynamics.
